chapters.title: Rental Boyfriend
chapters.html:
In the heart of the bustling city, nestled between glass towers and high-end boutiques, lived Mydeimos, a man who had it all.

At 35 years old, he was the picture of modern success: heir to the colossal Kremnos Corporation, sharp in both business and appearance, commanding boardrooms by day and hosting charity galas by night. His life was well-ordered, cleanly lined, and meticulously composed... Except for one thing.

Love.

Not that he hadn’t experienced something close to it.

He had. In fact, he had been harboring feelings for his childhood best friend, Hephaestion, for as long as he could remember. They had grown up together, attended the same elite schools, supported each other through adolescence and career climbs. They knew each other's coffee orders and worst fears, laughed at the same inside jokes, and saw each other as constants in a world that always changed.

But that was exactly the problem.

They were too close. Too familiar. The kind of bond where crossing the line into romance risked toppling the entire foundation of their connection. And Mydei, so rational, so careful, could never bring himself to gamble that away.

So, he slowly wiped the feeling away and, consequently, stayed single. He was busy enough with work. No time for distraction.

Until one night.

Mydei sat across from his old crush, as polished as always in a tailored black suit, gold cufflinks catching the light. Hephaestion, ever relaxed in his open-collared shirt and blazer, handed him a pale ivory envelope with a sheepish smile.

“My wedding is next month,” he said. “Don’t say I didn’t invite you properly.”

Mydei raised an eyebrow, taking the invitation between two fingers like it might combust.

“Formal wedding invitation?” he asked. “Is this your way of showing off?”

“Naturally,” Hephaestion chuckled. “But also because she insisted. She wants you to have it. You’re practically family.”

Mydei said nothing at first, just traced the foil-printed names. Their union looked permanent, no longer up for debate.

“Alright. I'll come,” he said finally, setting it down.

“I'll drag you by force if you don't,” Hephaestion smiled. Then, after a pause, he leaned back, his tone turning softer. “You know, Dei. I’ve been thinking.”

“That sounds dangerous.”

“Haha. No, really.” He scratched his head, sheepishly. “Once I get married, I’ll be wrapped up in the whole domestic thing. I won’t be around as much. And you, you’ve always been alone.”

Mydei looked up, scowled.

Hephaestion gave him a look halfway between concern and exasperation. “Don’t give me that face. You know I’ve been worried about you for years. You work yourself to death, avoid anyone who even flirts with you, and your idea of a break is...what? Reading quarterly reports in your jacuzzi?”

“I have hobbies,” Mydei said mildly annoyed.

“Right. Brooding doesn’t count.” Hephaestion sighed. “I just, I don’t want you to get lonely when I’m not around as much. You deserve someone too, Dei.”

Mydei’s composure cracked, not from anger, but something smaller, more brittle. His throat worked, but no words came.

So he lied.

“I’m not alone,” he said, his voice was steadier than what he felt.

“Huh?”

Mydei cleared his throat. “I’ve... been seeing someone.”

“Wait, you're serious?” Hephaestion laughed, genuinely delighted. “That’s great! Why didn’t you tell me sooner?”

Mydei avoided his gaze, trying to salvage his own trap. “It’s still new. He’s... younger. But we're going steady. He gives me space when I need it and supports me when I don’t realize I do.” His tone smoothed into faux confidence. “Keeps me grounded. Energized.”

Hephaestion looked downright gleeful. “Well damn. I’m proud of you. I’d love to meet him. Bring him to the wedding, yeah?”

“...Of course.”

They parted soon after, and Mydei didn’t even make it to his car before regret hit him like a slap. He leaned against the door of the black sedan, arms crossed.

He couldn’t believe what he just said.

( Younger? Supportive? What was that? An ideal boyfriend from a wet dream? )

He was still stewing in regret when he passed by a group of younger office workers exiting a café. They laughed among themselves, one of them scrolling on their phone and showing the others.

“...you know those rental boyfriends? I swear, they actually work. My cousin used one and said the guy was hotter than her ex.”

“No way,” someone snorted. “Don’t those guys charge a fortune?”

“Yeah, but they’re like professional. You can customize the type you want! Like clingy, aloof, smart, flirty. It’s wild.”

Their voices faded, but the damage was done.

Mydei’s eye twitched.

He slid into his car, lips pressed together.

“...Customizable, huh?”

His phone was in his hand before he even realised it. A search bar opened, then closed. Then opened again. He stared at it.

He could come clean to Hephaestion. Or pretend there was a sudden breakup...

Or...

He muttered under his breath, “...I hate myself.”

And typed: rental boyfriend near me.

The late afternoon sun draped the café in a warm, golden hue. The clink of cups and hum of conversation filled the space, but Mydei barely noticed any of it. He sat at a corner table, dressed in neat suit, back straight, fingers drumming a rhythmless beat against his cappuccino. He hadn’t touched it.

Maybe this was stupid. Maybe he should just leave, email Hephaestion an apology, feign a breakup and...

“Ah, you’re Mydei, right?” a bright voice chimed. “Sorry, I made you wait!”

Mydei blinked up and then froze.

The young man standing before him had the kind of smile that could split storm clouds. His silver-blue hair was a little messy from the wind, his eyes sparkled like a summer sky, and the moment he slid into the seat across from Mydei, the entire café seemed to tilt a little brighter, like someone turned up the saturation on reality. His aura was pure sunshine, cheerful, unbothered, naturally affectionate.

He did asked for an energetic man, basically the polar opposite of Hephaestion. But, he didn’t expect they would come up with someone with exact description.

“I’m Phainon!” he beamed. “Nice to meet you. I’ll be your boyfriend from now on!”

Mydei stared.

Phainon didn’t seem fazed. He clasped his hands together on the table, leaning forward just slightly, chin resting on the back of his hand.

“By the way, I’m twenty-two. College student. History of Art major.”

Mydei opened his mouth to say something, but only managed a stiff nod. “...Nice to meet you.”

He cleared his throat, internally trying to pull himself together. This was business. Temporary, performative affection. He should at least introduce himself properly.

“I’m...”

“Oh, no need!” Phainon cut in, waving a hand with a grin. “I already memorized your profile. Full name, job, favorite drink, likes exercise, your three sizes are—oh wait, I wasn’t supposed to say that one, huh?”

Mydei blinked. “You... memorized it?”

Phainon shrugged, grinning as if it were the most natural thing in the world. “It’s my job to know my client, right? And besides, you’re kinda unforgettable.”

That made Mydei pause.

A flustered silence fell, and Mydei found himself staring at the half-melted foam of his untouched cappuccino. “You don’t mind?” he asked, timidly now. “The age difference. It’s a bit significant.”

Phainon tilted his head, eyes twinkling with mischief. “Mind? Nope, you’re exactly my type.”

He winked.

Mydei, who hadn’t blushed since decades, could feel the slow crawl of heat creep up the back of his neck and flush his ears.

“...I see,” he muttered.

Phainon leaned back with a triumphant grin. “You’re cute when you’re flustered.”

"Don't tease me."

"Haha, sorry. Can't help it." Phainon grinned.

“So,” he then said, leaning forward, “how about we test the waters? A trial date. Just to see if you really want to keep using my service or if you wanna swap me out for someone taller, maybe buffer, or, heaven forbid, less charming.”

Mydei raised a brow. “Is this your tactic? Guilt-tripping clients into keeping you?”

Phainon beamed. “Only the cute ones.”

A small smile tugged at the corners of Mydei’s lips despite himself. He folded his coat over his arm and stood. “Alright. A trial date, then.”

Phainon perked up instantly, springing from his seat with the kind of ease only youth and sugar could afford. “Great! Do you wanna plan it, or should I lead?”

Mydei hesitated, fingers brushing the rim of his coat sleeve. “I, think I’ll leave it to you.”

“Oh?” Phainon tilted his head, curiosity dancing in his eyes. “You seem like the type who’d have a ten-year plan for everything.”

“I usually do,” Mydei admitted, cheeks lightly flushed. “But this would be my first date, so...”

Phainon stopped mid-step.

He turned with a dramatic gasp, pointing an accusatory finger at him. “You’re lying.”

Mydei blinked, startled. “I’m not.”

“There is absolutely no way that someone who looks like that” Phainon gestured at him from head to toe, “has never been on a date. You’re the walking poster boy for drama. Like, stock market by day, heartbreak by night.”

Mydei let out a small, low chuckle, rubbing the back of his neck. “I’ve been busy. Running a company doesn’t exactly leave much room for distractions.”

"So, that's why you look for our service to accompany you than actually find a real partner?"

"Precisely."

“Hmm, interesting. Then, why a younger man? Is there a reason for your preference?"

Mydei turned away, lips curved into a lopsided smile. "Who knows."

Phainon gave a low whistle, trotting up to fall into step beside him. “Oh, you’re dangerous when you smile like that.”

Mydei didn’t reply, but the soft blush lingering on his cheek gave him away.

Their casual date unfolded like a scene from a mellow rom-com.

Phainon took the charge, started from movies. He didn’t ask what genre Mydei liked. He simply dragged him into a horror movie premiere, declaring, “You look like the kind of man who never flinches. Let’s test that theory.”

Mydei, true to reputation, barely blinked through the screaming ghosts and sudden cuts. The only thing that startled him more than once was Phainon’s occasional jumps. And the way Phainon screamed, not from fear, but from sheer surprise, was the real entertainment.

“You’re worse than the girl next to us,” Mydei murmured, dryly amused as he handed him a napkin for the soda spill Phainon caused during a jump scare.

“She had a boyfriend to cling to,” Phainon pouted, gripping his cup.

“You have me, right?”

“...Don't jump scare me with being sweet all of sudden, Mydei."

After the movie, Phainon pulled him along to a quiet alley stall lined with warm lights and crepe banners fluttering in the wind. “This place is viral on social media,” he said, already placing orders for two. “Apparently the chocolate banana one has magical serotonin.”

Mydei didn’t comment, but Phainon noticed how his eyes lingered on the strawberry cream option. He added that to their order without a word.

They stood side by side, nibbling on their sweets as the wind brushed past. Mydei didn’t talk much, but Phainon filled the silence with cheerful hums and comments about the food, the lights, the tacky horror film. At some point, they naturally slipped into walking again, soft steps echoing under the warm street lamps.

“So,” Phainon started, licking whipped cream from his lip, “how okay are you with skinship?”

Mydei glanced at him, wary. “Define ‘okay'.”

“Like, okay with holding hands? Hugs? Being clinged on?” Phainon tilted his head. “I mean, I’m your boyfriend on paper. Gotta sell the illusion, right?”

Mydei hesitated, thinking. “I suppose I’m somewhat okay with it. I can do polite hugs. Social embraces.”

Phainon lit up like a kid on Christmas morning. “Perfect.”

And without further warning, he clung to Mydei’s arm. His entire body warm and soft against Mydei’s sharp lines. Mydei stiffened, immediately.

It was like hugging a marble statue. A very expensive, well-dressed statue.

“You good there?” Phainon asked, peeking up.

“Why wouldn't I be?” Mydei replied, deadpan.

Phainon laughed, loud and bright, tightening his grip as they walked. “Haha. We definitely need to work on your skinship. You look like I just tried to rob you, not being affectionate.”

Mydei sighed but made no move to pull away. He even relaxed a little, just a bit, just enough for Phainon to notice.

“Progress,” Phainon whispered smugly.

“I'm trying,” Mydei muttered, the corners of his lips twitched upward.

And so they walked, the older man’s face faintly pink, and the younger one grinning as if he’d won the lottery.

The city was winding down as the night fell, neon signs flickering to life, casting a soft glow on the station platform where Mydei and Phainon stood. The sound of an approaching train echoed in the distance.

“So,” Phainon said, rocking on his heels, his voice still carrying that casual cheer even as the night air cooled. “We'll be lovers until the wedding, huh?”

Mydei nodded, his hands tucked in his coat pockets. “That’s the arrangement.”

Phainon pulled out his phone. “Then we should exchange numbers. For professional reasons, of course.”

Mydei gave a dry chuckle, pulling out his own device. “Of course,” he repeated as they traded contact info.

A short silence followed, just enough for the wind to ruffle their coats. Then Phainon smiled again, gentler this time. “Say, could we meet somewhere private sometime later?”

Mydei furrowed his brows. “Private?”

Phainon tilted his head innocently. “Mhm. Not for any weird reason, really. I mean, maybe a quiet café or your place or something. I just think, if we’re going to be lovers, we need to work on our chemistry.”

That made Mydei pause. He wasn’t sure if it was the word chemistry or the sparkle in Phainon’s eyes that made his throat tighten. He swallowed, his voice remained calm but a little quieter. “Next weekend. I’ll pick you up here.”

“Really?” Phainon beamed. “Alright, deal!”

And just like that, the train pulled in. The doors opened, and with a final grin and a two-fingered salute, Phainon hopped on. Mydei stood there, watching the train until it blurred past, his thoughts trailing like the fading taillights.

He exhaled slowly.

( What have I gotten myself into? )

Despite a few days still left until the weekend, Phainon didn’t exactly disappear.

In fact, he was everywhere. His name blinked on Mydei’s phone screen almost religiously.

The first message came just past dawn.

Phainon: Good morning, Mr. Boyfriend 💙💙
Attached: A photo of Phainon holding up a breakfast toast, face squished in a sleepy pout.

At first, Mydei thought it was just part of the package. A charming routine from a rental boyfriend.

But it didn’t stop.

He got midday updates of latte art. Evening photos of city lights with captions like “you’d like this spot, I think."

Nighttime voice messages of a sleepy Phainon muttering “Good night, dream of me.”

Sometimes, Phainon would call.

Their first real call had started with awkward formalities but somehow lasted almost an hour. It shifted from talking about music tastes to complaining about commercials, and even to what kind of pets they’d raise if they ever had one.

Mydei told himself this easy rhythm was Phainon doing his job, crafting a seamless connection like a real lover would. Charming. Approachable. Disarming.

And then, the awkwardness between them thinned, replaced by something more natural. Something that almost felt normal.

Mydei would glance at his phone in board meetings now, lips twitching when he read some terrible pun Phainon texted him mid-presentation. And every night, when the ‘good night’ message came in, he stared at it a little longer than necessary.

Professional, he reminded himself.

Except his chest warmed anyway.

The weekend finally arrived, clear-skied and warm.

Mydei dressed casually. Fitted dark jeans, a button-down shirt with the sleeves rolled, and a fine wristwatch glinting on his wrist. He looked effortlessly elegant as he pulled up in his black two-seater and parked at the designated spot near the train station. The car gleamed like ink under the sun, clean and quiet as it idled.

Then, he saw him.

Phainon stood by the curb, scrolling through his phone, dressed in an explosion of color. Soft greens, layered with sunflower yellow and a scarf patterned in indigo swirls. The outfit shouldn’t have worked, and yet, it did. It fit him. Youthful, bold, and warm.

Mydei rolled the window down.

“Phainon,” he called softly.

Phainon’s head snapped up. His entire face lit up like a morning sun, and if Mydei squinted, he could’ve sworn he saw imaginary puppy ears perk up and a tail wagging behind him.

“Coming!” Phainon chirped, practically skipping his way toward the car. He hopped in with a wide grin, the scent of citrus and clean soap trailing after him.

“You look so different today,” he said, eyes scanning Mydei’s outfit appreciatively. “Way more relaxed. Honestly, I was starting to think you were fused to your suits.”

Mydei gave a short chuckle. “It was weekday. I came from work when we met.”

“Well, this fits our agenda much better,” Phainon teased. “Y’know, dating and all that.”

“I suppose I’m appropriately dressed then.”

They pulled out of the lot, the radio humming softly in the background. Phainon talked with his usual energy. About a group presentation for one of his courses, how someone messed up the slides, and the utter tragedy of pastries being overpriced on campus.

“So, History of Art, right?” Mydei asked at one point, glancing over during a red light.

“Yeah!” Phainon’s face lit up again. “I wanna be an appraiser, like, in museums or maybe for private collections. Antiques fascinate me, y’know? They’ve got stories layered into them. Like reading a book without pages. Just scratches, fading paint, and all.”

Mydei hummed in interest. “That’s... unexpectedly poetic.”

Phainon laughed. “What, doesn’t fit my image? I get that a lot.”

“It’s unique,” Mydei said simply.

Phainon grinned, clearly pleased. “Well, I like it. I want to learn how to see the invisible fingerprints people leave on things.”

They arrived shortly after, the two-seater pulling smoothly in front of a high-end restaurant tucked between taller buildings. It looked closed. No light in the windows, no valet at the entrance.

Phainon blinked. “Did you reserve the wrong date?”

Mydei got out and walked around to open the door for him. “No. It’s open.”

“But...”

“It’s mine,” Mydei explained, adjusting the cuff of his shirt. “I closed it for today.”

Phainon stopped mid-step. “Wait. You own this place?”

“Mm.” Mydei gave him a side glance. “I like to cook. I helped design the kitchen and I created most of the menu.”

“Oh wow.” Phainon looped his arm around Mydei’s again, grinning up at him. “Is there something that my capable lover couldn't do?”

Mydei stiffened at the sudden warmth against his side but didn’t pull away this time. After a second, his muscles relaxed, and he let out a breathless chuckle.

They walked into the empty restaurant, the gentle clack of Phainon’s boots and Mydei’s shoes echoing slightly in the quiet, elegant space. Everything was prepped, clean, the table set for two in front of a large window framing a private garden.

Mydei pulled out a chair with practiced grace and gestured for Phainon to sit. “Wait here. I’ll serve the food.”

“Wait, you’re not making me wait alone, are you?” Phainon asked playfully, craning his neck as Mydei started toward the kitchen. 
“Did your staff call in sick or something?”

“I gave them the day off,” Mydei said without turning around. “I didn’t want strangers hovering around during our... date.”

Phainon beamed, the word date buzzing pleasantly in his ears. He quickly stood up. 

“Then I’m helping.”

Mydei glanced back. “You’re a guest.”

Phainon shrugged, already rolling up his sleeves. “Then let’s make it a date where the guest also hauls food like a part-timer.”

Despite the initial protest, Mydei didn’t stop him.

Together, they carried the full-course meal, beautifully plated dishes already pre-prepared and kept warm, into the private dining room. Appetizers, mains, desserts. Every plate was presented with elegance and symmetry, from delicate beef carpaccio drizzled with balsamic pearls to raspberry pavlova resting on a dusting of gold sugar.

Phainon stared at the spread, eyes wide. “Did you make all this?”

“I had time this morning.”

“This morning??” Phainon exclaimed, mouth falling open. “You made all of this today?? Alone?”

Mydei gave a quiet nod, brushing nonexistent dust off his cuff. “It’s nothing too complex.”

Phainon looked at the meal again, utterly awed. “This is insane. You’re amazing! Can you stop being perfect for a day?”

He was rewarded with a sheepish smile and a faint pink dusting Mydei’s ears. It was brief, like a crack in a carefully polished statue. 

They sat. The meal began.

Phainon, of course, couldn’t just eat in silence. He talked between bites, enthusiastic and expressive, shifting the atmosphere to something warmer and less formal. He praised the beef. He hummed in delight at the truffle risotto.

Then he started pushing his luck.

First, it was the casual brushing of fingers when he passed a napkin. Mydei flinched, then frowned, but didn’t pull back.

Then, halfway through the meal, Phainon caught Mydei mid-reach for a side dish and gently took his hand.

“Warm hands,” he murmured, half-flirty, half-observant.

Mydei stared at him like he was short-circuiting. “You’re being very forward.”

“We do need to work on our chemistry,” Phainon said with a grin, giving the fingers a small squeeze.

“Chemistry doesn’t require holding hands during meal,” Mydei replied dryly, but he didn’t pull away. He even let their hands rest together for a moment longer before carefully reclaiming his fork.

But Phainon wasn’t done.

Next came dessert, the raspberry pavlova. Phainon took a bite, made a show of enjoying it, and then casually reached over with his spoon toward Mydei.

“Here. Try mine. I added extra syrup on this bite.”

“We have the same thing.”

“Still, try mine."

Mydei looked at the spoon, at Phainon’s expectant eyes, and sighed. He leaned forward slightly and accepted the spoonful. His lips closed around it neatly.

Phainon didn’t hide the flush on his cheeks or the little wiggle in his seat.

“That was adorable.”

“You exaggerate.”

“I understate,” Phainon teased. “You have this very princely way of being flustered.”

Mydei lowered his gaze to his dessert. “It’s not flattering to say I’m flustered.”

“But it’s cute.”

“I’m not trying to be.”

“I know,” Phainon said gently, with a sincerity that made Mydei glance at him. "Still, you're so cute."

"You have a weird scale to determine cuteness."

"I know, but I'm proud of my sense."

Mydei scoffed but he couldn’t hide his soft smile.

The meal ended with lingering forks and a shared silence. The clatter of dishes faded into the background, leaving only the low hum of the city beyond the glass. They moved to a loveseat near the tall windows, bathed in golden light from the sunset.

Phainon tucked his legs beneath him, sitting sideways on the couch while Mydei sat stiff and proper beside him, one hand on his knee.

“We should probably figure out how we met,” Phainon started, breaking the silence with a sheepish grin. “For the wedding.”

Mydei glanced at him, then back at the skyline. “Right. That would be wise.”

They lapsed into a short pause before Phainon perked up. “What if I was drunk? Like super drunk. And I almost tripped into the street. And then, bam! You showed up and saved me like a romance drama hero.”

“That sounds too dramatic.”

“Fine, then I was just mildly drunk and disoriented, and you helped me get a taxi. Less romantic, more believable.”

“And why would I help a drunk stranger?” Mydei arched a brow.

“Because I was beautiful and pathetic,” Phainon said without shame, placing a hand on his chest. “You have a kind heart. You couldn't leave me.”

Mydei exhaled in something halfway between amusement and disbelief. “Fine. I helped you. You sobered up. And?”

Phainon grinned. “Then I fell in love. You left your information, just in case and I used it to message you constantly. Sent you flowers. Asked you out relentlessly. You rejected me five times.”

Mydei raised an eyebrow. “Only five?”

“Okay, ten. But the eleventh time, you said yes. And we’ve been dating for three months now. New, but serious.”

Mydei hummed in thought, then gave a small nod. “That works.”

For a moment, they sat in silence again, watching the lights flicker on across the cityscape.

Then Phainon leaned in slightly, whispering softly now. “Since we’re serious, maybe we should try kissing?”

Mydei turned so fast his spine clicked. “Wh, why would we do that?”

Phainon tilted his head innocently. “Because... it’d be weird if we’ve been dating for three months and never kissed, right? I mean, chemistry-wise. People will expect it.”

Mydei opened his mouth to retort but closed it just as quickly. “That, makes some sense,” he admitted reluctantly, clearly debating with himself. He didn’t know how people usually progress, after all.

Phainon watched him, expression more tender now. “Have you ever kissed anyone before?”

Mydei shook his head slowly. “No.”

Phainon blinked, then softened even more. “Would it be okay if... I become your first?”

Mydei’s fingers tightened slightly around his knee. He looked away, then back at Phainon. His lips parted, uncertain, but finally, he gave a small nod.

The tension grew, warm and electric. Mydei’s breath caught in his throat as Phainon leaned in, slowly, as if giving him every chance to back away.

He didn’t.

Their foreheads brushed first, gently. Then Phainon tilted his head, closing the distance.

The kiss was soft, barely a brush of lips, uncertain and slow. But it lingered. A first kiss, warm and trembling, on a quiet evening between strangers who tried to play-lovers.

When they pulled apart, Mydei’s ears were brighter, his eyes slightly wider than usual.

The first kiss left the air shimmering between them, fragile and warm. Mydei looked dazed, eyes still half-lidded, his breath just a little uneven. His hands were stiff in his lap, fingers curled tight around the fabric of his trousers.

“...That wasn’t terrible,” he said quietly.

Phainon smiled, breathless. “Good."

Phainon, on the other hand, leaned back just a little, just enough to look at him properly. His eyes were soft, unreadable in the low amber light.

“...Can I kiss you again?” he asked, coaxing or maybe more like pleading. “Please?"

Mydei's eyelashes fluttered once, slow. Then gave the tiniest nod.

Phainon smiled. He moved closer, one hand lifting to gently cradle Mydei’s cheek. His thumb brushed along the cheekbone, featherlight, and Mydei’s eyelashes fluttered at the touch. Then Phainon leaned in again, slower, like this was something sacred.

Their lips met again, getting warmer. Deeper. Mydei's breath caught when Phainon tilted his head and kissed him more firmly, drawing him in with subtle pressure. Then he felt it, a soft tug, a wet warmth as Phainon gently suckled on his lower lip.

A soft, startled grunt escaped Mydei before he could stop it.

Phainon chuckled into the kiss. “Part your lips for me?” he whispered, so low and gentle it felt more like a plea than a command.

Mydei hesitated. A second. Two. Then, he obeyed.

And Phainon kissed him again, this time deeper. Their mouths met fully, open and wet and searching. Mydei tensed at first when he felt Phainon's tongue brushing softly against his own, unsure and unfamiliar with the sensation. But Phainon slowed down, coaxing, guiding, not rushing him. There was no demand in his touch, only a quiet encouragement. And soon, Mydei tried to respond, a little clumsy, a little stiff, but earnest.

Phainon's hand moved to cup his jaw now, thumb caressing the edge of his ear, fingers threading lightly into Mydei’s hair. Their mouths moved together, slow and sensual, the rhythm gentle but growing more sure. Mydei was learning. And Phainon was more than willing to teach.

The kiss lingered. Warm. Wet. A bit messy. And filled with a kind of heat that crawled beneath the skin and settled in the chest like a living thing.

By the time they parted, Mydei's lips were kiss-bitten and slightly red. His breath came in quiet pants, and there was a flicker of something raw and vulnerable in his golden eyes.

"So?" Phainon asked, smiling.

“...That was,” Mydei started, but he stuttering in the middle and he had to clear his throat to recover. “...new.”

Phainon laughed softly, his forehead gently resting against Mydei’s, his thumb gently wiped the trace of their kisses on Mydei's lips. “Good new, or awkward new?”

Mydei exhaled, his cheeks blooming with warmth. “...Both.”

Phainon grinned. “Then we’re getting somewhere.”

Days passed like pages turning gently in a novel Mydei wasn’t quite ready to finish.

Their chats continued. Frequent, lighthearted, sometimes silly. Phainon would send blurry selfies from campus, short voice notes of him complaining about professors, random snapshots of antiques in museums captioned with things like “This urn reminded me of your judgmental stare 🥹”.

Mydei would reply after meetings, in between boardroom decisions and luncheons with shareholders. His answers were sometimes curt, sometimes dry, but never cold. He had begun to share things, too. Pictures of the sunset outside his office window, quiet recordings of piano pieces he liked, even a rare photo of himself. Phainon always noticed the smallest things. “Your sleeve’s wrinkled, did you nap in your office again?”

Mydei was still as busy as ever, often tied up in meetings and reports, but he always carved time out for Phainon. Even if it was just late at night, bleary-eyed, suit jacket tossed over his couch as they talked over video call while Phainon lay sideways across his bed in colorful pajamas.

The weekends, however, were always cleared for their dates.

They went to the gym together once. Mydei, who had always preferred solitary training, found himself matching pace with Phainon. What began as light sparring turned competitive fast. Phainon was agile and annoyingly enthusiastic, and Mydei, despite telling himself not to indulge, ended up trying harder than he should’ve, just to not lose.

“You’re such a tryhard,” Phainon panted, grinning as they jogged back to the showers.

“You started it,” Mydei replied, deadpan but his lips curved, just a little.

It became a pattern. Mini competitions. Who could make the basketball shot in fewer tries. Who could get a higher score in games at the arcade. Who could run faster uphill during jogs. There was laughter, light teasing, and the growing comfort of familiarity. Mydei also started to share his house, inviting Phainon for simple meal or just lazy day in front of his home theatre.

Skinship also came easier now. Hugs felt less like rehearsals and more like instinct. He no longer flinched when Phainon leaned against his side while they watched silly videos on his couch, or when Phainon looped their arms together as they walked in the city. Mydei also touched Phainon with ease, like stroking Phainon's thigh while he read the report while the young one played on phone or just as simple as ruffling his fluffy hair to calm him down.

Once, during a lazy Sunday, Phainon randomly asked, “Can I braid your hair?” and after a long pause, Mydei silently handed him a comb and turned around.

Phainon’s fingers were gentle. He didn’t say anything embarrassing, not out loud anyway, just hummed while working, but Mydei could feel the smile in his touch.

Even the kisses became routine. A quick kiss as a hello. A stolen peck after a shared meal. Sometimes Phainon would lean in, cheekily closing his eyes. “Can I get one moral support?”

Mydei would glance around, then kiss him, once, twice, less hesitant each time.

Their parting kisses at the end of their date also had shifted from tentative brushes to lingering ones that left Mydei staring at his steering wheel with his fingers pressed against his lips.

Somewhere between the gentle teasing, the easy laughter, the familiar cadence of Phainon’s voice echoing through late-night calls, Mydei felt it.

The shift.

The silent sinking.

He caught himself rereading old messages and started saving photos of Phainon like they were important. He noticed the way Phainon’s eyes crinkled when he was genuinely happy. He found himself thinking about him during idle moments, wondering what he was doing, if he’d eaten, if he was warm enough.

He started looking forward to weekends. Not just because he get to rest, but because he’d see Phainon again.

And somewhere between the walks, the lazy chats, the competitive banter, and the kisses he had grown to crave...

The line was blurred.

And he was falling.

Falling into something he told himself was supposed to be fake.

Falling for someone who, technically, was paid to smile for him, to treat him well. To kiss him good.

And every time his heart fluttered, he smothered it quickly.

Don’t fall too deep.

This is a service.

A role.

An arrangement.

Not love.

He couldn’t afford to desire something that would never be real.

Two weeks left before the wedding. Mydei decided to get custom-made suits for them, especially after heard Phainon didn’t have formal attire. Phainon refused at first but Mydei reminded him that Phainon would be his prestige as well. Not that he didn't like his fashion sense, or that he looked down on him but people would judge eitherway. He didn’t want anyone to say anything bad to Phainon just because some designer's clothes.

Phainon reluctantly agreed.

One week left and the clothes were ready for final fitting. They decided to meet up in the evening because Mydei had important meeting in the morning.

It was supposed to be just another meeting. Numbers, reports, polite smiles exchanged over a high-end lunch. The hotel’s lounge was quiet, refined, filled with the sound of soft jazz and murmured conversation. Mydei sat at the head of the table, his posture flawless, his tie perfect, his voice calm as he discussed quarterly forecasts with poised authority.

Until something, someone, caught his eye.

Across the spacious lobby, beneath the warm amber lights, walked a figure that made his heart falter.

He blinked once, twice, as if his mind was playing tricks on him.

Phainon.

Not the usual Phainon in pastel knits and oversized sweaters, arms wrapped around him like ivy, bubbling with mischief. No. This Phainon wore a sleek jacket in muted tones, fitted slacks, his usually playful hair styled with care. He looked taller somehow. Colder. Sharper.

And he wasn’t alone.

There was a woman beside him. Beautiful, her hand wrapped around his arm with a familiarity that dug like thorns into Mydei’s chest. She leaned in, whispered something close to his ear, and Phainon smiled, that smile. The one Mydei had quietly memorized, the one that softened his world without even trying.

The pair walked to the front desk. A brief exchange. A room key was handed over.

Mydei’s heart sank.

Then came the elevator. The quiet chime, the slow, ceremonial close of its doors. Gone.

The world around him blurred. The numbers on the report stopped making sense. The voices at the table faded beneath the rush of blood in his ears.

He shouldn’t be this shaken.

He shouldn’t be surprised.

He knew what Phainon was. A rental boyfriend. A service. A transaction dressed in the illusion of affection.

He knew.

But logic never had much to do with the heart, did it?

Logic didn’t stop the ache.

It didn’t stop the way his hands curled into fists under the table. Or the hollow that bloomed in his chest like something had gouged itself out.

He had warned himself, so many times. Don’t fall too deep. Don’t get used to the warmth. Don’t believe the illusion.

But he also allowed himself to believe, just a little. To feel, just a little too much. He thought maybe, just maybe, the warmth Phainon offered wasn’t part of the script. That the kisses, the laughter, the late-night calls had started to mean something real.

The truth hurts. He was just a role. A name on a form. A paycheck.

Mydei realized just how stupid he’d been.

Because this wasn’t betrayal.

It was just reality.

Phainon had never been his.

He straightened his spine and finished the meeting with a smile no one could tell was cracked.

Later at night, they met just outside the boutique, where the streetlights bathed everything in a soft golden glow. Phainon approached with his usual grin, bright and bold, dressed in a splash of colors like he was sun incarnate. A loose patterned shirt tucked into wide-legged pants, mismatched sneakers that somehow made sense on him, and a crossbody bag swinging with every hop in his step.

Mydei greeted him as calm as always but for Phainon, who could notice any slightest change when Mydei didn’t even notice it himself, frowned a little.

Phainon didn’t press, at least not right then.

They entered the boutique together, where their tailored suits awaited. The tailor greeted them and led them into a fitting room draped in mirrors and warm light. And there, hung side by side, were the results of weeks of fittings and adjustments.

Phainon’s suit was a clean white ensemble trimmed with delicate black embroidery along the collar and sleeves, modern but playful, refined but soft around the edge, just like him. He looked like a fresh breeze in spring, the smile on his lips lifting the entire room.

Mydei’s was the reverse. Black with subtle white accents threading the cuffs and lapels. Sharp, elegant, powerful. He stood like a statue carved from obsidian, the kind people admired but dared not touch.

“Damn,” Phainon said when he looked into the mirror, standing beside Mydei. “We look good. Like scandalously good. I’d marry us.”

Mydei chuckled quietly, but the warmth didn’t quite reach his eyes.

Afterwards, Mydei offered to drive Phainon to the station. The ride was silent, broken only by soft music humming from the car’s speakers.

The silence pressed heavier with each passing streetlight.

Mydei glanced at him. “What is?”

Mydei kept his eyes on the road. “Does it matter?”

“Huh?”

Mydei regretted it the moment the words left his mouth.

It was cruel. Uncalled for. But he didn’t know how to stop the sharp edge in his tone from bleeding through.

Phainon didn’t respond immediately. When he did, his smile looked the same on the surface, but the edges had crumpled like paper left in the rain.

“Right,” Phainon said, his voice dropped too soft to be real. “Of course. Sorry for being nosy.”

He turned to look out the window, and Mydei couldn’t bring himself to say what he should have.

Not when he’d already drawn the line with his own hand.

The goodbye that night had been stilted and hollow, like the final note of a song that rang flat. Phainon still gave his usual “take care” before closing the door, but the words had a brittle edge. Not angry. Not accusing. But he sounded sad and it hurted Mydei the most.

Phainon still texted afterwards. Still sent random photos of the sky, of a snack he found cute, of a cat he saw lounging on a car hood. But the messages were different now. Shorter. No emojis. No spark. It was like he was only doing his job.

Mydei responded. He didn’t left Phainon on read, he would never do that. Still, he couldn't just act like nothing happened so his respond was worsen than convo-killer.

One afternoon, Mydei opened his phone to a message that simply read:

Phainon: Do you want me to stop texting you?

He stared at it for a long time. The three dots blinked once from his side. Then vanished. Then he replied two hours later with:

Mydei: I'm sorry. I was busy.

What a liar. Busy was his middle name but he always got time for Phainon.

And Phainon definitely knew that so he didn’t send any follow up. No more unnecessary text even after days passed.

The days that followed passed like torture. Mydei buried himself in work, took longer shifts, scheduled unnecessary meetings. Anything to keep himself too busy to think. Too busy to feel. But the ache didn’t care for logic or distractions. It just sat there in his chest, heavy and constant.

Until the wedding.

It was a two-day and one-night cruise. Intimate and extravagant, the kind of thing Hephaestion always joked was “extra,” but secretly adored. The yacht was strung with warm lights, the sea stretched endlessly around them, and champagne flowed like water. Mydei stood tall and composed, dressed sharply, smiling where needed.

And Phainon was brilliant.

He played the perfect lover so well, Mydei almost forgot it was all just a role. As if nothing happened between them, Phainon stayed next to him like a clingy guy he supposed to be. He smiled at Mydei, touched his shoulder casually, offered him drinks before he could even ask. He posed for photos, complimented Mydei in front of guests, and even wrangled conversations with Mydei’s colleagues and friends like he’d known them for years.

“My boyfriend is so amazing, isn’t he?” Phainon beamed to one of Mydei’s university friends, fingers lightly looped through Mydei’s arm. “You know, sometimes I wonder if he’s even real.”

Mydei played along, smiling, answering with his usual grace, even slipping in soft gestures here and there. His hand on Phainon’s back. A chuckle whispered into his ear.

He knew it was all just for show.

He knew.

But that didn’t stop his heart from beating faster when Phainon leaned into him, touching his cheek, or a simple as how their fingers entwined. It didn’t stop the way his chest ached every time he caught the golden curve of Phainon’s smile under the fairy lights.

Because no matter how much he reminded himself it was fake, it didn’t feel fake.

Not to him.

His feeling wasn't fake.

And that’s what hurt the most.

It was 3 a.m. when they returned to the cabin.

The party officially ended today and they were on the way back to the shore. Gone were the clinks of champagne flutes, the mellow laughter under gold-drenched lanterns, the rhythm of heels against the yacht deck. Now it was just them, standing in a room soaked in silence, interrupted only by the soft hum of the air conditioner.

Mydei loosened his collar, walked to the counter, and uncapped a decanter of Whiskey. No glass, he poured it directly into his mouth, the liquid burning down his throat. His back was tense, his shoulders drawn in like armor. He didn’t like alcohol, he never liked it but he felt he needed some before he crashed.

Phainon hovered by the bed, shifting awkwardly before slowly sitting down on the edge. His fingers curled against the hem of his blazer.

“So,” he said, gently pierced the heavy air around them, “I guess this is our final scene, huh?”

Mydei didn’t look back. He simply nodded.

Phainon let out a breathless laugh, fingers fidgeting with the rings he wore tonight. “We probably won’t meet again after this, right?”

Mydei said nothing. The silence between them started to ache.

After another brief silence, Phainon stood, rubbing his arms, suddenly unsure of himself. “Did I do something wrong?”

Mydei finally turned his head, brows furrowing.

Phainon met his gaze but his smile was vulnerable. “I mean, you definitely changed. Did I hurt you somehow? Or annoy you? Or say something I shouldn’t have?” He paused. “If I did, I’m sorry. I just I wish you’d tell me.”

Mydei shook his head. “It’s not about you,” he muttered. “It’s my own problem.”

He lifted the whiskey again, but before the bottle touched his lips, Phainon stepped forward, too fast, a little desperate, and placed his hand on Mydei’s wrist, gently halting him.

“You already drank too much,” Phainon said softly.

Mydei’s jaw clenched. “Why would you care?”

There was no venom in the words. Just exhaustion. Frustration. Pain, hidden under a mask he wore far too long.

“Is it written in the contract?” he continued, “That you have to care about me that much?”

Phainon’s breath caught, his lashes flickering like he’d been struck.

He gave a shaky smile. “No. That’s not in the contract.”

He looked down, then back up, his voice was softer now, stripped of pretense. “You probably won’t believe me, and maybe I don’t deserve your trust, but...” His fingers tightened slightly around Mydei’s wrist. “At some point, I stopped thinking of you as just a client.”

The words lingered in the air, trembling and vulnerable.

“I don’t know when exactly,” Phainon continued. “Maybe when you told me you never dated before. Or when you tried so hard not to flinch when I hugged you. Or when you let me kiss you, even if you were shy and nervous.” His voice cracked a little. “Maybe because you earnestly tried to be a good boyfriend for me. Every time. You made me feel confortable.”

He exhaled. “And I started wanting to be someone more. Not just someone you hired.”

Mydei stared at him, expression remained unreadable. Inside, his chest felt tight, like something soft and fragile was struggling to beat its wings beneath his ribs.

Phainon’s smile faltered, but he didn’t step away. He gently peeled the bottle from Mydei’s hand and set it aside with a soft clink. Without a word, he took Mydei’s hand, gently grasped it and slowly guided him to sit down on the bed.

The mattress dipped beneath their weight. The silence was heavy, like fog on the sea.

Phainon didn’t let go. He sat close, shoulders brushing, fingers lacing carefully with Mydei’s. His grip wasn’t tight. Steady enough to keep them both anchored.

“I won't ask you to believe me,” Phainon said. “And I get it. This whole thing started with money. You were supposed to be a client. I was supposed to be a professional.”

He glanced down, then up again with a small, self-deprecating smile. “But I really like you, Mydei. Not as your rental boyfriend, not because you paid me or because I had to play a part. I just really fell for you. Somewhere along the line. Or maybe from the start.”

He gave a soft chuckle, shaking his head. “Gosh, I’m such a failure at this job. But in my defense, you were my first client. And, well, my only one.”

That made Mydei’s brows knit together. “Your first?”

Phainon nodded. “Yeah. I was struggling with tuition and rent, and my friend knew someone at the agency. Said it paid well. So I signed up, thinking I could fake my way through a couple of months.”

He laughed again, more to himself now. “I should’ve backed out the moment I saw you. You were just too much my type.”

Mydei turned to look at him, stunned. “You never said...”

“Because I thought I could keep it together,” Phainon murmured. “Thought I could stay professional. But every time you laughed at my jokes, or tried to relax when I hugged you, or blushed when I kissed you. I lost a bit more of the script.”

“I saw you,” he murmured. “The same day with our fitting. At the hotel lobby.”

Phainon blinked.

“You were with someone,” Mydei added, eyes dropping to their entwined hands. “A woman. You were smiling. You took the key and went upstairs together.”

Then his expression shifted—startled, then confused. “Wait, what? That day?”

Mydei nodded once.

Phainon frowned. “That’s not possible. I had an exam that day. Right before the fitting. I told you, remember? I even sent you a picture of the exam hall.”

“Oh, okay, I think I know what’s going on.”

Phainon reached for his phone and began tapping something. “I didn’t mention this before because, well, I didn’t think it was important. But, ” he turned the screen toward Mydei, “I have a twin brother.”

Mydei’s eyes widened. “What?”

Mydei’s eyes flicked up, holding his gaze. “But I might consider kissing a full-time one.”

Phainon’s lips parted. “Are you asking me to quit?”

Mydei shrugged one shoulder, trying not to look too affected. “If you want to, well, stay with me, then yeah. No more part-timing as someone else’s boyfriend. Just be mine.”

“I’ll quit,” he said, no hesitation. “I’ll figure out another job later. But right now...”

Phainon murmured his name between kisses, like a prayer spoken only in twilight.

Their mouths parted just enough to breathe, then met again with a need that no longer pretended to be hidden. The scrape of Mydei’s fingernails down Phainon’s back made him shiver. Mydei tugged at his shirt with quiet insistence, and Phainon obliged, sitting up slightly to take it off. The cabin’s warm air kissed the sweat on his skin.

Mydei frowned. “I’m not—”

“You are,” Phainon insisted, thumb brushing over the faint crease between Mydei’s brows. “You’re so, so beautiful. And adorable.”

I love the way your brows furrow when you’re embarrassed.” A kiss to the bridge of his nose. “The way your ears turn red.” A kiss to the corner of his mouth. “The way you look at me like you want to deny everything and still let me in.”

Mydei’s fingers twitched. His throat bobbed with a swallow.

He moved as if learning, tracing tenderly, sometimes teasing, all while murmuring small praises that made Mydei cover his face with his arm.

Phainon’s breath was warm against his cheek. “Past kisses. I, I want to... But only if you’re okay with it.”

He nodded. “Yes, it's okay.”

What followed was slow, burning, tender. 

Phainon moved with so much care it nearly made Mydei ache. Each kiss, each press of his fingers, meant to ease the tension, to light up every nerve. The room filled with musical of carnal desire. The creak of the bed. The slap of skin. The soft rustle of sheets and the distant hum of the ocean outside. Mydei’s voice, whether it was quiet curses, breathless pleas, whimpers that only Phainon could coax out of him, everything was the most beautiful sound Phainon had ever heard.

The shadows thrown across the wall shifted with their rhythm, two shapes, one moving slow and deep, the other arched into him, head thrown back. Their rhythm quickened, deepened, became a language of its own, as if they'd done this a hundred times before. 

Phainon's hand found Mydei's, fingers lacing together above the pillow as their foreheads touched. His other hand anchored Mydei's hip, guiding him through the rising tide.

"Mydei..." Phainon’s call cracked with whisper which too full of everything, too much feeling.

Mydei gasped his name in return, the syllables strung on trembling breath. His eyes fluttered open for a moment, gaze glazed. His cheeks were flushed, a pink that bled down his throat, and his body moved to meet Phainon like it couldn’t stand to be apart for even a second.

The coil of heat built steadily between them, unhurried, like waves lapping higher and higher. Phainon's mouth found Mydei's jaw, then the corner of his lips, then lower, pressing kisses like promises on every place he could reach.

“You’re so beautiful,” Phainon murmured. “I wish you could see yourself through my eyes.”

Their fingers squeezed tighter, their breath tangled, and Phainon angled his hips just right, earning a cry from Mydei that tipped him over the edge. Mydei’s back curved, trembled, a broken moan escaping him as his whole body seized and shimmered with release. He clung to Phainon, chest pressed tight, hips shaking from the force of it.

Phainon followed moments after, lost to the feeling of Mydei beneath him, warm, welcoming, beloved. His breath caught in his throat, forehead pressed to Mydei’s temple as the waves crashed through him as well.

When the tension gradually dimmed, it left them gasping and tangled together, hearts pounding.

Phainon didn’t move right away. He was still inside him, arms caging around Mydei’s body, his lips pressed gently to the crook of his neck.

Mydei’s voice was barely a whisper. "You’re heavy."

"I know," Phainon murmured, not moving.

"You’re still inside."

"Also true."

Mydei let out a breathy chuckle. "I’m serious. I can’t feel my lower half."

"That’s a compliment."

"Phainon..."

"Nope," Phainon said, grinning as he started kissing down the side of his neck again. "Not done yet."

Mydei groaned, thumping a weak fist against his shoulder.

“You just finished.”

Phainon’s fingers gently traced the edge of his jaw. “I know. But you feel too good. And you're soo beautiful when you’re like this. Please?"

Mydei stared at Phainon. His hair was a tousled mess, cheeks flushed in a post-bliss glow, but what really got to Mydei was the expression.

Phainon’s lower lip jutted out slightly, his brows tilted up in that unmistakable pleading slope, eyes wide and glimmering with innocence and lust all at once. He looked utterly ridiculous, adorable, but ridiculous.

And for a second, Mydei swore he could see a pair of drooping dog ears flopping low, and a sad little tail giving one slow, pathetic wag behind him.

“Don’t give me that face.”

Phainon tilted his head, adorably. “What face?”

Mydei cursed under his breath and pulled a pillow over his face. He peeked out only to say, “...Never mind. Just slow down this time. I’m not made of steel.”

Phainon lit up instantly, eyes sparkling like the damn sunrise behind him. The imaginary tail wagged faster.

He kissed Mydei’s hand first, then his lips, featherlight and reverent. “I’ll go slow,” he promised, even as his fingers began to explore again, already coaxing warmth to rise from skin that still ached from the last round.

This time, there were no rushed gasps, no stumble of urgency, only sighs shared between breaths and kisses given like praise. Mydei's quiet moans were drawn out with purpose, until his limbs curled again around Phainon, his name falling from his lips in a voice softer than the sea outside their window.

The room was filled with the sound of skin meeting skin, of whispered names, of heat rising again, and again, and again.

Until finally, the pale blue hue of dawn crept over the horizon, slipping through the curtains in gentle slants of gold.

Only by then the two united hearts were beating in sync, finally drowned in peaceful slumber.

The morning sun spilled golden across the deck as the cruise finally docked at the harbor. Mydei stood near the railing, hands in the pocket of his slacks, talking quietly with Hephaestion while the soft bustle of guests preparing to disembark hummed behind them.

“Once again,” Mydei said, offering a small, sincere smile, “congratulations. You really looked happy.”

Hephaestion gave him a lopsided grin, loosening his tie a bit. “Thanks. And you too.”

Mydei blinked. “Me?”

“Yeah.” Hephaestion glanced out to sea for a second, then back at him. “I’ll be honest, I was a little worried at first when I saw your boyfriend. He’s so young, and well, so bright. Kind of loud. I thought he might be some clingy kid trying to use you.”

Mydei scoffed, “He’s in college. What use I have for him?"

"Your money?"

"Hah, do you think I'm that stupid?"

“No but people in love is often losing their brain capacity. That was what a very close friend of mine used to say.” Hephaestion teased and Mydei rolled his eyes in response.

“But,” his tone softened, “watching you two together, it’s obvious. He really likes you. And you,” he gave Mydei a knowing look, “you look at him like he's someone precious. I’ve never seen you like that.”

Heat crept up Mydei’s neck, but before he could protest, a sudden weight leaned into him from behind.

Phainon had snuck up, arms looping loosely around Mydei’s middle. “What are you two conspiring about?” he chirped, cheek pressed to Mydei’s shoulder. His hair was messy from the wind, but his smile was impossibly bright.

“Nothing too scandalous,” Hephaestion chuckled. “Nice to meet you again, Phainon. Please take care of him, alright?”

Phainon raised a thumb with dramatic flair. “Always!”

They parted with casual waves and laughter. Mydei and Phainon made their way down the ramp, shoes clicking gently against the harbor path.

The wind brushed gently through Mydei’s coat. His hand was linked with Phainon’s, fingers tangled easily like it had always been that way. He looked down at their joined hands.

He had expected to feel... something. Bitterness, maybe. Pain. A tight pang of what-ifs about Hephaestion.

But there was nothing.

No ache, no longing. Only warmth. Only Phainon’s bright presence at his side, tugging his heart into the present.

It was strange, he mused. That nothing about Hephaestion had even crossed his mind during any of his dates. That he hadn’t once compared them. Phainon had simply filled his world without trying.

He caught himself smiling.

“What’s funny?” Phainon asked, tilting his head to look up at him.

Mydei shook his head, cheeks slightly pink. “Just thinking. I might like you more than I realised.”

Phainon gasped, eyes wide with mock surprise. “Oh? Is that your roundabout way to ask me for sleeping with you again?”

Mydei sputtered, his ears flushing. “Wha—?! No!”

But Phainon only cackled, tugging Mydei closer by the wrist. “Too late. I'll take it that way.”

“I didn’t imply anything as such!”

“I don't care. I'll still doing it once we're alone.”

“Phainon, you—!”

He was silenced with a kiss, Phainon’s grin pressing into his mouth. It was warm, playful, and yet deep enough to stir Mydei’s chest.

And as the world bustled around them, the sun rising behind the docked ship, Mydei closed his eyes and kissed him back.
